approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from a bounded population of high-scoring accepted molecules. It draws parents from score quantiles and fills a surplus pool through connected-fragment crossover, optional finishing mutation and local graph mutation walks. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identities, duplicate rejection and a narrow sulfur-environment gate control admission; the sulfur reference is the maximum signature count across the original scored generating parents. A Gaussian process refitted to the complete accepted archive uses integer Morgan counts and generalized Tanimoto similarity. Correlated score draws select distinct pool members, and real feedback updates both the archive and the greedy survivor population.
approach.novelty: Test a synthetic-pretrained TabPFN ranking mean inside this existing sampled allocator. A fixed Gaussian projection makes the count rows small enough for the original released regressor, which predicts from all current real observations without updating its weights. Its predicted mean replaces the allocation score location while the original Gaussian residual law remains active. Completed siblings changed kernels, fitted radius or composition, or removed uncertainty; the earlier bootstrap-tree experiment learned locally and changed both the learner and uncertainty. This tests a pretrained response algorithm with its necessary adapter as one intervention. Concurrent siblings change batch selection or pool breadth, so their results remain separate comparisons against the same Parent.

observed_bottleneck: The one limiting behavior is low, inconsistently productive allocation from the fresh offspring field: useful archive learning and many breeding uses do not reliably yield better absolute offspring or productive later alternatives. The actual three Parent n-1744a1494180 summary.json/run.log pairs are complete and successful, with mean 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878 and seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287 and 0.583088384937917. Its change against its own Parent is only +0.0007834645552323346, including a losing third seed. The current-Parent audit published with n-f04cec6ab705 records only 648 strict best-generating-parent beats among 4350 offspring, 255 sequential incumbent advances, mean offspring score 0.372049560842182 versus best-generating-parent score 0.4553040448335957, and 343 of 636 later-used parent-winning sources without a productive direct descendant. The Parent molecular report describes persistent local families alongside real independent alternatives, so global scaffold collapse is not established. Ranking capability is an unresolved intervention target rather than an identified mediator. The likelihood-fitted composition sibling n-5cc22bb8f56b improved same-label ordering yet lost 0.013060374701989693 at the complete endpoint; fitted radius n-3f67db7b3d96 lost 0.03999213099436901. These are direct warnings that fit/ranking gains need not produce endpoint gain. Mean-only allocation n-f04cec6ab705 lost 0.11631688199011732 and correlation removal n-8df0bb3bbcfe lost 0.05054466462284635 on this exact Parent, supporting retention of the original nonzero correlated residuals. Historical bootstrap CART n-7922cfd1903a lost 0.0609765636321587 against an earlier ungated Parent and replaced uncertainty jointly; it was not a pretrained foundation-model test. No supplied Parent artifact is missing.

literature_review.conclusion: Adopt the admitted original synthetic-pretrained TabPFN-v2 regression mean through the declared fixed128 Gaussian count adapter and retain the complete current Parent GP covariance/residual law. The primary small-data report, official pinned model card, public wheel metadata and inspected download-disabled API support this as a feasible construction hypothesis. TabPFN-2.5 contains both synthetic-only and real-data variants, so its default cannot define this asset; do not upgrade. Defer TabICLv2 on its documented 300-row lower pretraining boundary and 2-to-100-column range relative to the active 10-to-290-row contexts. The projection is necessary to fit the original v2 500-feature interface and can discard signal, so no isolated foundation or projection contribution is registered. The current protocol and candidate-bundles document permit the construction, superseding the earlier model/package ban; actual offline loading, transitive binary wheels and issued-resource feasibility still need bound-node preflight. I performed the listed searches in this PLAN and read the supplied r30-search-policy receipts separately; their inherited queries are not listed as my searches. Direct Nature full-page/PDF fetches redirected and direct PMC opening was challenged, so the relevant indexed primary article methods/limitations and official releases supplied the reading. The narrow 2.1.3/500/download search produced no additional useful primary source; direct official release metadata and actual public-wheel inspection supplied that feasibility evidence. General tabular gains and documented synthetic training establish neither adaptive molecular-search gain nor an independent contamination audit. The complete prospective panel will decide the fixed recipe.

finding_summary.headline: TabPFN changes allocation but worsens prospective ranking; more local wins do not deliver stronger search
finding_summary.insights: This recipe clears the earlier practical obstacle: a pinned synthetic-pretrained model can condition on every accepted row and change real molecular allocation offline within the issued resources. That successful integration does not establish useful ranking transfer. The passive original GP orders the exact Child-selected labels better, so the result rules out the intended intermediate ranking improvement on this observed stream without mixing different search histories. More novel cores and more sources with improving descendants coexist with lower absolute quality and smaller cumulative gain; novelty and local parent wins alone are weak progress proxies here. The chemistry makes that distinction concrete: accepted streams still include compact useful carbonyl and amine arrangements, but often grow elaborate rings and appendages while retaining reactive bonds and incomplete stereochemical identity. These associations do not identify the cause of the loss or imply a universal filter. Projection, pinned preprocessing and pretrained response priors remain one coordinated test; separate contribution and global or counterfactual ranking are unresolved.
finding_summary.results: The pretrained model ran in all 15 sessions and changed 2,994 of 4,350 selection positions while preserving the original correlated GP residual law. Its predicted ranking benefit failed on the same accepted molecules: mean squared error rose from 0.00655 to 0.00742, within-batch ordering accuracy fell from 68.94% to 63.49%, and mean Spearman correlation fell from 0.484 to 0.353. Fourteen of 15 sessions lost ordering accuracy and correlation. Local parent wins increased from 648 to 703 and sequential incumbent advances from 255 to 268, but accepted scores and advance magnitudes were lower. The complete Child endpoint mean was 0.54477 versus Parent 0.59645, a descriptive difference of -0.05168; 14 of 15 endpoints and all three seed means were lower. The official comparison has no compatible seed pairs because the Child adds 23 packages to the Parent’s 43-package lock, so the registered profile-matched +0.002 efficacy criterion remains unevaluable. The Parent’s late deco_hop breakthrough remains in the primary panel; descriptive sensitivity also stays negative.

molecular.headline: Carbonyl-rich aromatic frameworks and cyclic amines grow elaborate, while reactive attachments and stereochemical gaps persist
molecular.overall_character: Node n-3062f0c87203 produces compact aromatic ketones/amides, linked nitrogen-rich diones, halogenated aryl/cyclic amines, aryl-linked dicarbonyl nitrogen rings, and fluorinated carbonyl/imine systems. Rings are abundant. Aromatic character is rich across the whole panel, but it is not universal: a leading fluorinated dicarbonyl family is entirely nonaromatic. Distinct seed families and many connected ring graphs support moderate overall diversity; leading series nevertheless often retain a core and vary substituents or appendages. All 15 Child and 15 published n-1744a1494180 Parent trajectories were present and read. Each node supplies 900 records per objective, including 870 accepted optimizer observations; no task or trajectory path is missing. These are accepted Search streams, not evidence about rejected or unselected generated molecules. Complete Child coverage is distinct from Parent pairing: context.comparison has child_complete=true, paired_complete=false, matched_seeds=[] and profile_mismatched_seeds=[0,1,2]. The receipts expose the environment difference. Child dependency_lock_sha256 is cd5e2bf850a0e1fb99a312762f14443e6523281d1ee06a0c771adc668e8e2de0 and Parent is 28728e9c5fff9004bafeb6c1336164bb198c744403ef36ca6454040cb0f61d78; the actual staging and published requirements.lock files match these hashes. The comparison profile includes environment_lock_hash. All six execution receipts share the same resource profile_hash, and summaries retain batch ten, ten initial observations, budget 300 per objective and 1500 calls per replica. Published Parent chemistry and labels below are descriptive historical references, not compatible paired performance evidence. In fixed task order, Child median heavy-atom counts are 25, 57, 39, 34 and 27, versus Parent 24, 31, 29, 31 and 27. Child median RDKit-perceived ring counts are 3, 8, 6, 5 and 4. Digest ring-closure-string incidence spans 0.9379 to 1.0; aromatic-string incidence spans 0.6598 to 1.0. These are molecule-level text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Charge-marker and stereocentre-marker incidence is 0.0 throughout, although available amines and potentially stereogenic centres are present. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 parsing has no descriptor failures and finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2664 Child accepted optimizer observations versus Parent 2455, with no assigned tetrahedral observations in either stream. Recognizable amides, ketones and cyclic amines coexist with direct heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxide links, N-S/N-N connections, aromatic-labelled large rings and densely connected or highly elaborated structures. Those features make overall synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak, with substantial molecule-to-molecule variation. Labels do not establish stability, conformational access, synthesis or pharmacology. Structural descriptors and all path hashes are in .slots/L01-resume-20261003/r30-slot0-molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json; receipt evidence is in that directory's profile_receipt_audit.json. Every cited complete SMILES is in the Child digest or its trusted Search trajectories. Qualitative gap provenance is retained from Development n-c55c3d520a2c through profile-1 n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180; this report re-observes output chemistry under the Child's changed Candidate environment and does not pool historical effects or attribute chemistry to a component.

per_task.generated_character: Leaders are compact fused aromatic carbonyl compounds with aryl partners. Seed 0's 24-heavy-atom leader has an adjacent aromatic N-N region, an O-containing fused ring and an aminophenyl ketone, without a direct N/O-halogen bond. Seed 1's 24-heavy-atom leader retains an indole-like pyridyl carboxamide with ring N-F and ethyl substituents. Seed 2's 25-heavy-atom diaryl ketone carries methylamino and ring N-amino groups plus a chloromethyl ether. Across accepted output the median size is 25 heavy atoms and the median perceived ring count is 3. Familiar aromatic/carbonyl chemistry is present, but the N-F, N-N and halomethyl environments need separate local assessment.
liabilities: Direct N-F and halomethyl ether environments raise local stability and synthesis questions; they are distinct from ordinary aryl fluorination and from the adjacent aromatic nitrogens in the seed-0 heterocycle.
The cyclic peroxide and heavily elaborated thioamide-containing proposal retain graph validity but lack the useful compact context of the leaders.
missing_features: Conventional peripheral substitution is not consistently retained with the favorable compact aromatic/carbonyl relationship: N-F, ring N-amino and chloromethyl ether attachments occur among leaders. A non-N/O-halogen ketone family is already available.
Independent plausible realizations of that favorable arrangement remain limited among leading series; the trajectories establish no exact missing target pharmacophore.

A small cyclic peroxide scores 0.0, bromomethane 3.0022306134138205e-20, and a 45-heavy-atom elaborated indole/thioamide proposal 3.315183114286997e-17. The visible association is a compact complete aromatic/carbonyl arrangement, rather than an obligatory amide: ketone leaders also have useful labels. Published Parent endpoints are 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596, 0.4369542269692598, from compact azaaryl-amide or adjacent thiocarbonyl/carbonyl families. per_task.generated_character: The accepted stream is heavily elaborated: median 57 heavy atoms and 8 perceived rings, versus historical Parent medians 31 and 4, with Child maximum 118 heavy atoms. Seed 0's 52-heavy-atom leader joins multiple nitrogen/carbonyl regions through an N-N connection, with an azaaryl terminus and a branched unsaturated chain. Seed 1's 56-heavy-atom leader has linked dione/azaaryl regions, a long polyene/enone appendage, an ester and small ring closures. Seed 2's 65-heavy-atom leader joins several azaaryl/oxygen-ring regions to a carbonyl-rich chain bearing N-O and N-Cl connections. All accepted optimizer observations have aromatic-string and ring-closure-string incidence. Sulfur is uncommon here, in 39 observations versus historical Parent 333; its absence does not make the large connected structures conventionally plausible.
liabilities: N-Cl and N-O/N-N links require environment-specific assessment, while multiple carbonyl and unsaturated regions add synthesis and stability questions.

Small closures, complex linked heterocycles and long unsaturated appendages coexist with large molecular size. Equal labels for several appendage variants do not establish the whole framework's synthetic feasibility.
missing_features: Compact, independently plausible alternatives preserving the favorable linked nitrogen/carbonyl organization are not consistently established at the leading labels; all three Child seed leaders remain highly elaborated.

Credible geometry and specified alkene/imine or stereochemical identity are not established for the polyene and densely connected families. The record identifies no exact target scaffold that a task-agnostic generator should be forced to make.

Child endpoints are 0.6206044082990619, 0.6097885126545707, 0.6069783711304145. The seed-0 polyene, ene-yne and shorter methyl-branched relatives at evaluations 268, 278 and 286 all score 0.6206044082990619, so additional terminal unsaturation is not supported as necessary by those labels. The published Parent endpoints are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6204376881838878, 0.6442339647723496; its high-label compact carbonyl/thione arrangement reached at evaluation 281 is not recovered by these larger Child families. The score gradient rewards specific linked heterocyclic context beyond small fragments, but does not support aromatic mass or elaborate appendages as intrinsically beneficial. The Parent comparison is descriptive and profile-incompatible.

per_task.generated_character: Leaders combine halogenated aryl regions with available cyclic or aliphatic amines. Seed 0's 25-heavy-atom leader has phenol, a fused saturated carbocycle and a chlorinated azetidine side chain. Seed 1's 34-heavy-atom leader has connected/spiro nitrogen rings, an aminomethyl group, aryl sulfur and an O-Cl substituent. Seed 2's 35-heavy-atom leader has a connected aryl/cyclophane-like framework with two N-methyl azetidine groups, phenol and carbon-bound halogens, without direct N/O-halogen bonds. Useful amine chemistry is already present, alongside extensive elaboration and reactive local bonds.
liabilities: O-Cl substitution, halogenated amine-adjacent carbons, peroxide links and difficult connected topology require distinct local assessments. Ordinary aryl halogens and saturated azetidines should not be conflated with those concerns.

There are 160 O-halogen and 113 O-O-containing Child optimizer observations versus historical Parent 75 and 8. Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 866 of 870 Child observations. These counts describe chemistry, not a paired effect or a toxicity measurement.

Stereochemical and conformational identity remain unresolved: the three Child leaders have respectively one, three and three RDKit-perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres.

Leaders include an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring, densely connected small closures, aryl/cyclophane-like arrangements and connected medium nitrogen rings. The Child has 11 cyclic-cumulene observations versus historical Parent 6, while no ring alkynes are observed versus Parent 13. Those are distinct motifs, not a general geometry improvement. Recognizable cyclic amines and compact aromatic carbonyl compounds remain available.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish representable ring graphs from credible unsaturation and connected topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make transformations sensitive to ring size, unsaturation and bridge connectivity, and provide feasible alternatives retaining learned functional relationships. Aromatic labels and sanitization do not provide conformational evidence. Avoid a blanket prohibition of small, fused or medium rings; no causal score benefit is established here.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original qualitative source n-c55c3d520a2c in Development, carried through profile-1 n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180. Re-observed in n-3062f0c87203 on issued Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 at batch ten and 300 observations per objective under its changed Candidate dependency environment; Parent chemistry is a profile-incompatible descriptive reference. Every Child digest stereocentre-string incidence is zero. RDKit finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2664 of 4350 Child accepted optimizer observations versus historical Parent 2455, and no assigned tetrahedral observations. A cyclic-amine leader has three unassigned centres, while some compact aromatic carbonyl leaders have none. The fluorinated nonaromatic leader also has unassigned centres; the gap applies where a structure requires stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic molecular arrangements remain incompletely specified after generation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemical identity when meaningful, treating symmetry and configurational instability appropriately. Assess alkene/imine geometry, tautomerism and protonation separately. The observed omission establishes neither a stereochemical score penalty nor a component-specific origin.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original qualitative source n-c55c3d520a2c in Development, carried through profile-1 n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180. Re-observed in n-3062f0c87203 on issued Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 at batch ten and 300 observations per objective under its changed Candidate dependency environment; Parent chemistry is a profile-incompatible descriptive reference. Accepted Child streams have median sizes reaching 57 and 39 heavy atoms, versus historical Parent 31 and 29, and Child maxima reach 118 and 119. A 62-heavy-atom carbonyl concatenation has an extremely low label; several polyene/ene-yne appendage variants share a label. Tiny fragments are less prevalent: 30 Child accepted observations have at most three heavy atoms versus Parent 82, with none in three of the five streams. This re-observes unhelpful growth more strongly than widespread fragmentation, and compact useful ketone/amide, cyclic-amine and dicarbonyl arrangements remain available.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful functional-group context while controlling excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use current accepted feedback to preserve useful combinations of regions while simplifying, expanding or reconnecting graphs. Distinguish productive growth from redundant appendages rather than imposing a universal size cutoff or preferring more aromatic mass. This output association identifies neither the responsible operator nor a guaranteed endpoint benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original qualitative source n-c55c3d520a2c in Development, carried through profile-1 n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180. Re-observed in n-3062f0c87203 on issued Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 at batch ten and 300 observations per objective under its changed Candidate dependency environment; Parent chemistry is a profile-incompatible descriptive reference. Leading series repeatedly alter terminal unsaturation, halogen placement, short chains or ring closures on retained aromatic/carbonyl, cyclic-amine and nitrogen/dicarbonyl arrangements. Different seeds also reach ketone versus amide, aromatic versus nonaromatic dicarbonyl and distinct amine families, so useful coverage is locally limited rather than globally collapsed. Many typed cores and new strings coexist with difficult topology or excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.gap: Plausible independent alternatives to a leading local framework are not consistently represented among high-label molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer feasible scaffold changes retaining favorable functional relationships learned from current feedback, beyond peripheral decoration. Assess actual labels and chemical credibility separately. New strings or ring counts alone do not establish useful coverage, and these associations establish no component attribution or general benefit from more diversity.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
